chunks: Blessed is the soul that discharged its obligation to its Lord, and endured its hardship by its side, and forsook its sleep in the night,
until when sleep overpowered her, she lay down on the ground, and used her hand as a pillow,
among a group whose eyes stayed awake due to fear of their return (to God), whose sides turned away from their beds,
and their lips murmured with the remembrance of their Lord, and their sins were cleared away through their prolonged seeking of forgiveness.
They are the party of Allah; Be it known, verily the party of Allah alone shall be the successful ones
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of those who perform night prayer according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage, often cited as the 'Verse of Qiyam al-Layl' within Shia exegesis, vividly depicts the ascetic discipline of the night prayer, contrasting the physical discomfort of sleeping on the ground with the spiritual vigilance of those fearing the Hereafter. It serves as a direct commentary on Quran 58:22, framing the 'Party of God' not merely as a political group but as those who embody consistent devotion through night worship and repentance. The imagery of 'wearing out misery on their sides' highlights the tangible sacrifice of comfort for spiritual purification, a key theme in Shia ethical teachings.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Blessed is he who discharges his obligations towards Allāh and endures his hardships, allows himself no sleep in the night but when sleep overpowers him lies down on the ground using his hand as a pillow,
along with those who keep their eyes wakeful in fear of the Day of judgement,
whose bodies are ever away froth beds,
whose lips are humming in remembrance of Allāh and whose sins have been erased through their prolonged beseechings for forgiveness.
They are the party of Allāh; Be it known, verily the party of Allāh alone shall be the successful ones (Qur’ān, 58:22).
